title: Optimization of Early Postnatal Weight Monitoring in Newborns: Implementation and Evaluation of an Additional Weight Measurement at 24 Hours for More Accurate Determination of Reference Weight
summary:
This study investigates whether an additional weight measurement of newborns approximately 24 hours after birth helps to assess normal weight changes during the first days of life more accurately.
Currently, in routine clinical practice, newborns are weighed shortly after birth and again at approximately 48 hours of life. The additional weight measurement at approximately 24 hours is performed for study purposes only and does not influence medical care or clinical decision-making.
All newborns from 35 weeks of gestation onwards who are born at LMU University Hospital between February and May 2026 will be included. The collected data will be compared with existing routine data from the period before the introduction of the additional weight measurement.
The aim is to evaluate whether the additional weight measurement could help to improve the assessment of early postnatal weight development in newborns in the future.

interventions.name:
Newborns ≥ 35+0 weeks of gestation who are born between February 2026 and May 2026 at LMU University Hospital (Campus Großhadern and Campus Innenstadt) and are transferred to the postnatal ward after birth.
Within the study, an additional weight measurement will be performed for study purposes only

criteria:
Inclusion criteria:
Newborns with a gestational age ≥ 35+0 weeks, born at LMU University Hospital (Campus Großhadern or Campus Innenstadt) between February 2026 and May 2026, and transferred to a postnatal ward after birth. Documentation of weight measurements according to the study protocol (≤ 4 hours, 20–30 hours, and 48 hours postpartum).
Exclusion criteria:
Preterm newborns with a gestational age < 35+0 weeks and newborns who are transferred primarily or secondarily to a neonatal intensive care or intermediate care unit after birth.
